validity.recommendation: no structural change; ref-fill Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start/Location/Owner with the sources below; do NOT merge/collapse with P0925 (HVJ), P3297/P3299 (GREP-I/II) or P3298 (DVPL-II) -- documented distinct physical segments of one integrated system
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE/ATTRIBUTION all confirmed. Primary source: a GAIL (India) Ltd letter to the PNGRB Secretary dated 27.11.2018, 'Final Tariff Determination of HVJ-GREP-DVPL and DVPL/GREP Upgradation Natural Gas Pipeline Network of GAIL (India) Limited' (https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/public-notice/GAILLetter27.11.2018.pdf -- one of the gem.wiki page's own cited leads, chased and read directly). It is a scanned/image-only 7-page PDF (no text layer; url_verifier 200s and correctly reports every keyword missing -- confirmed manually by rendering all 7 pages with pdftoppm at 300dpi and reading them with tesseract OCR). Its Annexure-A, para 1.4, states verbatim: 'DVPL-I:- During the year 2004, in synchronization with commissioning of India's first LNG Regasification Terminal at Dahej by PLL, a 42"x 612 Km, Dahej-Vijaipur Pipeline (DVPL) of 23.9 MMSCMD capacity was built in the common RoU (from Vemar, Gujarat, to Vijaipur, M.P.) of the HVJ Pipeline.' This is GAIL's own first-party account, independent of GEM, and confirms: EXISTENCE (real, built, commissioned asset -- this is a formal regulatory filing, not marketing copy); StartYear1=2004 (exact match); PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas (a cross-country natural-gas trunk line feeding the HVJ system, same class as its siblings); Owner1=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% (GAIL is the filer and sole named entity for the whole HVJ-GREP-DVPL network throughout); StartLocation/EndLocation Dahej->Vijaipur is directionally correct, with the minor nuance that the letter names the physical tie-in point as 'Vemar, Gujarat' rather than 'Dahej' itself (Vemar is evidently the dispatch/RoU tie-in near the Dahej LNG terminal) -- not a material error, 'Dahej-Vijaipur' is the pipeline's own common/trade name used consistently by GAIL, GEM, and third parties. DUPLICATE check against the full 35-row India roster: DVPL-I is explicitly NOT the same pipe as its four siblings that make up the 'Integrated HVJ' system -- the same GAIL letter (para 1.3-1.5) and the current PNGRB monthly line-wise register (https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, edition 31 May 2026; large multi-column PDF, url_verifier false-negatives per the documented pattern, confirmed locally via `pdftotext -layout`) both independently corroborate that HVJ (1987, ~1800 km, since expanded/reported at other lengths), GREP-I (1997, 36in x 505 km, Vijaipur-Dadri = P3297), GREP-II/Upgradation Phase-I (2010, 48in x 505 km, Vijaipur-Dadri, parallel to GREP = P3299), DVPL-I (2004, 42in x 612 km, Dahej-Vijaipur = this row, P0919), and DVPL-II/Upgradation Phase-II (2013, 48in x 610 km, Dahej-Vijaipur, parallel to DVPL-I = P3298) are five physically distinct pipes sharing a common right-of-way and now operated/tariffed as one integrated network -- exactly the granularity split the sweep's own scope guidance anticipated; PNGRB's current register lists them as ONE combined asset ('Integrated HVJ', GAIL, authorised 6,169 km / operating 6,732 km / authorised+design capacity 111.3 MMSCMD, natural gas supplied 80.3 MMSCMD, 75.0% utilisation, May 2026). Wikipedia's 'HVJ Gas Pipeline' article (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HVJ_Gas_Pipeline, verified) independently confirms the system exists and is GAIL-owned/operated but its infobox only covers the original HVJ/GREP scope (length 3474 km, 36in, 33.4 MMSCMD) and never separately discusses DVPL -- consistent with, not contradicting, the above; not used as a numeric source for this row. Two independent-origin sources (GAIL's own regulatory filing + PNGRB's current regulatory register) corroborate existence/classification/ownership; tier high on those axes.

validity.recommendation: re-verify LengthKnown before relying on 770.00 km -- three sources give three different figures (GEM 770 km, GlobalData/offshore-technology 710 km, GAIL's own 2018 regulatory filing 612 km for the specific 42in Vemar/Dahej-Vijaipur line); also note Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD is the shared HVJ-GREP-DVPL SYSTEM total (identical value also carried on siblings P0925/P3297/P3298/P3299), not DVPL-I's own throughput, and is now stale vs the current PNGRB system figure
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC check on LengthKnown and Capacity. LENGTH: GEM carries LengthKnown=770.00 km for DVPL-I. GAIL's own 27.11.2018 letter to PNGRB (Annexure-A para 1.4, OCR-confirmed, see prior finding) states DVPL-I is specifically '42"x 612 Km' from Vemar, Gujarat to Vijaipur, M.P. -- a first-party, GEM-independent primary source that disagrees with the sheet by ~158 km (about 20%). A second, commercially independent source, GlobalData's Oil & Gas Pipelines database as republished by offshore-technology.com (https://www.offshore-technology.com/marketdata/dahej-vijaipur-gas-pipeline-india/, verified OK, contains 'Dahej' and '42'), gives yet a third figure: 'a 710km-long onshore pipeline... maximum diameter of 42 inches... started operations in 2004... owned by GAIL (India)'. So three sources -- GEM (770), GlobalData (710), GAIL-to-regulator (612) -- disagree with each other, none matching exactly; the spread (612-770) is materially large (~26%) and cannot be dismissed as rounding or a units slip. I could not locate a fourth, tie-breaking numeric source (Wikipedia's HVJ article does not itemize DVPL separately; PNGRB's current monthly register reports only the combined 6-pipe 'Integrated HVJ' system total of 6,169 authorised / 6,732 operating km, not the DVPL-I component alone; a GAIL EOI PDF that a web search summary claimed contained a 'HVJ 1179 / GREP-VDPL 456 / DVPL 610' breakdown was fetched and read directly -- that breakdown does NOT actually appear anywhere in the document, a hallucinated citation I am flagging and discarding rather than repeating). Given the disagreement, I am NOT proposing a replacement value; this needs a human decision on which figure (or which vintage/definition of the route) GEM should carry, so verdict=concern rather than a silent pass. CAPACITY: GEM's Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD/CapacityUnits=MMSCMD is IDENTICAL across all five components of the integrated system in the 35-row roster (P0919, P0925, P3297, P3298, P3299 all = 107.0) -- consistent with the sweep's known India pattern of GEM assigning the combined-system authorised capacity to each split component rather than that component's own individual throughput (DVPL-I's own original design capacity per the GAIL letter was 23.9 MMSCMD in 2004, since grown via later upgrades that are properly attributed to the other component rows). This is explainable/expected per the sweep's scope guidance (do not propose collapsing the rows), so not flagged as a duplicate defect, but it does mean 107.00 does not represent DVPL-I's own capacity and it is now stale versus the current PNGRB reading: the 31-May-2026 monthly register (link above) lists the 'Integrated HVJ' system's current Authorised/Design capacity as 111.3 MMSCMD (natural gas supplied 80.3 MMSCMD, 75.0% utilisation) -- a further ~4% drift beyond the shared-attribution issue. Noting both points for Update; not proposing an edit to Capacity myself since the correct fix (component-level split vs. system total, and which vintage) is a judgment call outside this sweep's scope.
